extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, and USPTO examiners (USPTO staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on acceptable signature types, formatting, authentication, certifications, internet/email communications, duplicate filings, and application/filing-receipt procedures for patent applications and related correspondence filed with the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of acceptable signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence filed with the Office which requires a person’s signature may be filed with one of three types of signatures: (A) handwritten signature; (B) 'S-signature'; and (C) Office Electronic Filing System (EFS) character coded signature. See 37 CFR 1.4(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that these are the only authorized signature types for correspondence requiring a signature; specifies that 37 CFR 1.4(d) does not authorize filing correspondence by e-mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handwritten signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A handwritten signature may be an original or a copy. 'Original' means personally signed in permanent dark ink or its equivalent by the person whose signature appears. Dark color is required for legibility when scanned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scanned images filed via EFS are permitted as a copy. Typewriter-applied signatures are not handwritten (and must meet S-signature rules). Electronic reproductions of handwritten signatures electronically applied are not treated as personally signed originals. Copies (including second-generation copies) are acceptable where copies are explicitly permitted, but an original should be retained as evidence if authenticity is questioned. Red ink or pencil are not acceptable as 'dark' or 'permanent'.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-signature format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An S-signature must consist only of letters or Arabic numerals or both, with appropriate spaces and commas, periods, apostrophes, or hyphens, and must be enclosed between a first single forward slash and a second single forward slash (e.g., /Dr. James T. Jones, Jr/).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-text graphic characters (e.g., smiley faces) are not permitted. Additional forward slashes are not permitted. Presentation of just letters/numerals without enclosing slashes will be treated as unsigned. Punctuation marks must be properly associated with letters or numerals; an S-signature of only punctuation is improper. Script fonts are not permitted for any portion of a document except the S-signature. Typed names in script font without slashes are treated as unsigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may insert an S-signature and how
rubrics_metrics.description: The person signing must insert his or her own S-signature by directly typing it via keyboard; one person may not type another person’s S-signature for them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person physically unable to use a keyboard may direct another person to press keys while simultaneously reviewing the document for signature. Knowingly adopting another's S-signature is not permitted. For consistency and to avoid doubt as to identity, the same S-signature should be used each time without variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner registration number with S-signature
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent practitioner (37 CFR 1.32(a)(1)) signing pursuant to 37 CFR 1.33(b)(1) or (b)(2) must supply his/her registration number either as part of the S-signature or immediately below or adjacent to the S-signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number character (#) may be used only as part of the S-signature when appearing before a practitioner’s registration number; otherwise the number character may not be used in an S-signature. When signing as an assignee or as an applicant (inventor) under 1.33(b)(3) or (b)(4), a registration number is not required and should not be supplied to avoid confusion as to signing capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed/typed name presentation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The signer’s name must be presented in printed or typed form preferably immediately below or adjacent to the S-signature and must be reasonably specific enough so the identity of the signer can be readily recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Printed or typed name may be applied by a typewriter or machine printer and may be inserted before or after the S-signature and does not have to be inserted by the S-signer. A printed or typed name in letterhead or elsewhere in the body of the document is not acceptable as the presentation of the S-signer's name.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS character-coded signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EFS character coded signatures (for correspondence submitted via EFS in character coded form) must consist only of letters of the English alphabet, or Arabic numerals, or both, with appropriate spaces and commas, periods, apostrophes, and hyphens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These signatures are inserted into EFS menus/forms (transmittal, assignment, declaration, power of attorney, fee transmittal, e-IDS, etc.). Scanned images of ink signatures and S-signatures may be filed as TIFF attachments and are distinguished in the EFS file list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications upon presentation of papers (37 CFR 10.18(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The presentation to the Office (whether by signing, filing, submitting, or later advocating) of any paper by a party (practitioner or non-practitioner) constitutes a certification under 37 CFR 10.18(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of 10.18(b)(2) may result in sanctions under 10.18(c); practitioners violating 10.18(b) may also be subject to disciplinary action (see 10.18(d) and 10.23(c)(15)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification as to signature of another (reasonable basis & evidence retention)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person submitting a document signed by another under 37 CFR 1.4(d)(2) or (d)(3) must have a reasonable basis to believe that the person whose signature is present actually inserted the signature, and should retain evidence of authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable basis does not require actual knowledge but some reason to believe the signature is appropriate (e.g., an executed declaration returned by the inventor). Where an assignee is involved, additional chain-of-custody evidence (e.g., email chain with attachments) may be required. Retain emails, cover letters, or other evidence showing transmission and execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-certification of inserted signature
rubrics_metrics.description: The person inserting a signature under 37 CFR 1.4(d)(2) or (d)(3) certifies that the inserted signature appearing in the document is his or her own signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibits one person from requesting a second person to insert the first person’s signature. The person requesting an inappropriate insertion may also be subject to sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for certification/signature violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of certifications as to the signature of another or a person’s own signature can result in sanctions under 37 CFR 10.18(c) and (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the inserter and requester may be subject to sanctions or disciplinary action; Office may require ratification, resubmission, or other remedies when authenticity is in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratification, confirmation, and evidence of authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Office has reasonable doubt as to signature authenticity (variations, mismatch with printed name, etc.), the Office may require ratification, confirmation (including submission of a duplicate properly signed document), or other evidence of authenticity such as a chain of custody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratification requires the person ratifying to state he/she personally signed the previously submitted document and, if needed, submit a compliant signature format. Confirmation means submitting a duplicate document with a compliant signature. Resubmission may be required if the signature image is illegible. Ratification cannot change the legal name of a signer (name changes must follow petition procedures). Inadvertent typographical errors usually treated as bona fide attempts and only require ratification when identity is in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of noncompliant S-signatures and unsigned-paper examples
rubrics_metrics.description: The inadvertent failure to follow S-signature format will be treated as a bona fide attempt but the paper will be considered unsigned; specific examples include: (A) S-signature not enclosed in forward slashes; (B) S-signature composed of non-text graphic characters; (C) S-signature not a name and no accompanying name adjacent or below to identify the signer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, after being required to ratify or resubmit, the signer repeats the same noncompliant S-signature, the reply will not be considered a bona fide attempt and no additional time will be given to correct it. Obvious typographical errors that do not create doubt as to identity need not trigger notice or further action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification originals required where statute mandates
rubrics_metrics.description: When a document that is required by statute to be certified (e.g., certified copy of a foreign patent application under 35 U.S.C. 119 or certified copy of an international application under 35 U.S.C. 365) must be filed, a copy (including photocopy or facsimile) of the certification is not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This original-certification requirement does not apply to certifications required under 37 CFR 1.8, since those are not statutory certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet/email confidentiality and authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: If security and confidentiality cannot be attained for a specific use, transaction, or activity, that use shall not be undertaken. Internet e-mail communications concerning information subject to confidentiality under 35 U.S.C. 122 require written authorization by the applicant for USPTO to communicate via e-mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Backup, archiving, and recovery of information sent/received via the Internet is the responsibility of individual users; OCIO does not normally provide backup/recovery for Internet-produced or -transmitted data. A written authorization may be withdrawn by filing a signed paper; withdrawal is effective when approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limits of Internet e-mail communications with USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications via Internet e-mail are at the discretion of the applicant; where written authorization exists, Internet e-mail may be used for communications other than matters under 35 U.S.C. 132 or matters that require a signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A paper copy of authorized Internet e-mail communications MUST be assigned a paper number, entered into PALM, and placed in the patent application file. Replies to Office actions may NOT be communicated via Internet e-mail (such e-mails will be placed in the file but marked NOT ENTERED). USPTO employees may not initiate e-mail communications with applicants unless written authorization is of record. Special rules apply for reissue applications and reexamination proceedings (employees may not initiate e-mail without authorization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of sender for Internet e-mail
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet e-mail must be initiated by a registered practitioner or an applicant in a pro se application, and must include sufficient information to show representative capacity in compliance with 37 CFR 1.34.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable indicia include attorney registration number, attorney docket number, and patent application number. Patent Organization users must be aware of spoofing risks and follow established procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of electronic mail services and interview restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: E-mail shall NOT be used to conduct exchanges similar to those in telephone or personal interviews unless written authorization has been given; where authorized, a paper copy of the e-mail contents MUST be made and placed in the patent application file (as required by the Federal Records Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Examiner who receives applicant e-mail may respond by telephone, fax, or other appropriate means; Internet e-mail is not an appropriate medium for formal interview-like exchanges absent authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate copies requirement for multiple files
rubrics_metrics.description: Since each file must be complete in itself, a separate copy of every paper to be filed in a patent, patent file, or other proceeding must be furnished for each file to which the paper pertains, even if contents are identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing duplicate copies should be avoided except where the Office requires duplicates. When duplicates are not required, filing multiple copies may delay processing and the Office may discard duplicate copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application number assignment and filing receipt content
rubrics_metrics.description: Application numbers (series code + serial number) are assigned by the Office of Initial Patent Examination (OIPE) immediately after mail is opened; the filing receipt informs applicant of application number and filing date (unless filed under certain provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing receipt includes application number, filing date, a four-digit confirmation number, a suggested class, and an art unit. Series codes identify application types (e.g., 01/11/ for nonprovisional utility/plant/reissue, 29/ for design, 60/ provisional, 90/ ex parte reexamination, 95/ inter partes reexamination). A postcard receipt gives preliminary assignment but should not be relied upon as the controlling application number. The confirmation number is used with the application number to verify accuracy on correspondence and must be used when submitting an EFS copy for publication; applicants are recommended to include the confirmation number on all correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return postcard itemization for filing receipt evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If a self-addressed postcard is submitted with a patent application for a receipt, the postcard should itemize all components of the application (applicant's name(s); title; number of pages of specification, claims, and drawing sheets; whether oath/declaration is included; list of additional forms; amount and manner of fee payment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the postcard does not itemize each component, it will not serve as evidence that any non-itemized component was received by the USPTO.
